summary: Nora keeps her image-generation logins alive on her own: both the xAI and the ChatGPT (Codex) login are refreshed at least once a day and before their access tokens expire, so asking for a picture after a quiet fortnight no longer finds the login dead.
details: Both logins are kept whenever image generation is on and the login's token is set, whichever provider is selected, so switching provider also finds a live login.
A refresh that fails now says so: every failure is logged with which login and why, and an alert fires when a login has not refreshed for two days or its token was refused.
A new `nora xai-login` now takes over from an old, dead login without anyone deleting a state file, the way the Codex login already did.
limitations: The keepalive keeps a login alive; it cannot revive one the provider has already refused, which still needs a new login.

Why that login died (unused too long, or revoked because another copy of the same token was used elsewhere) is not known; if two checkouts on one host hold the same token, a refresh in one can still log the other out.
